---
title: "html: column widths"
format: html
# `::: {.column width="40%"}` becomes an inline `width` (Pandoc's HTML writer
# does this itself; q2 does it in HtmlColumnsTransform), and the stylesheet
# lays `div.columns` out as a wrapping flex row so the columns sit side by
# side at those widths. A column with no width keeps the stylesheet default.
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - - 'div.columns > div.column[style="width: 40%;"]'
          - 'div.columns > div.column[style="width: 60%;"]'
          - 'div.columns > div.column[style="width: 30%; color: red;"]'
          - 'div.columns > div.column:not([style])'
        - - 'div.column[width]'
      ensureCssRegexMatches:
        - - 'div\.columns\s*\{[^}]*display:\s*flex[^}]*flex-wrap:\s*wrap'
          - 'div\.column\s*\{[^}]*width:\s*50%[^}]*min-width:\s*0'
        - []
---

## Two columns

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
COL-LEFT
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
COL-RIGHT
:::

::::

## A styled column and one with no width

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="30%" style="color: red;"}

:::

::: {.column}
COL-DEFAULT
:::

::::
